The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from GitHub using a tagged release archive over HTTPS: `source=("${pkgname}-${pkgver}.tgz::https://github.com/${_gitauthor}/${_gitname}/archive/${_gitversion}.tar.gz")`. The sha256sum is provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the source will be verified during fetch.

During the sourcing phase (which includes top-level variable assignments and any `pkgver()` function), no command substitutions or external executions are performed that could lead to arbitrary code execution. The `pkgver` is hard-coded as `1.3.0`, so no dynamic version fetching occurs. All variables are defined via simple string expansions or arrays, with no use of `$(...)` or backticks for command substitution at the top level or within `pkgver()`.

The commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` will safely download, verify, and extract the source archive without executing any build or prepare steps. Since `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` are not run under these flags, potentially dangerous operations inside them (if any) are not triggered. In this case, even those functions only perform standard operations like `sed`, `go mod tidy`, `make`, and file installation — all within the build directory and directed at legitimate package files.

Thus, running the specified makepkg commands on this PKGBUILD does not pose a risk of remote code execution, data exfiltration, or unintended system modification.
</details>
<summary>
No dangerous code in sourcing or source fetch
</summary>
</security_assessment>
